## Summary

**STOREI** (Store Indirect register into memory): Store 64 bit from indirect source register in memory.

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | `(d) → <vea>` |
| Syntax | `STOREI b,<vea>` |
| Short | Store 64 bit from indirect source register in memory |
| Description | Store is the AMMX equivalent of move dn,&lt;ea&gt;. For many cases, the normal store instruction is more appropriate and convenient. While this indexed variant requires to preload the index register, it helps for example at places where the source register is to be changed conditionally. Also, you may think of storing a list of AMMX registers in a loop instead of in a row to keep code size small (where appropriate). See also loadi. |
| Condition codes | not affected |

### Encoding

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–9 | `1111111` |
| 1 | 8 | A |
| 1 | 7 | B |
| 1 | 6 | `0` |
| 1 | 5–3 | Mode |
| 1 | 2–0 | Register |
| 2 | 15–12 | b |
| 2 | 11–0 | `000100000100` |

- Not allowed &lt;vea&gt; : #imm
- d: value =&gt; register

```text
  00 - 07 = D0  -  D7
  08 - 15 = A0  -  A7
  16 - 23 = B0  -  B7
  40 - 47 = E0  -  E7
  48 - 55 = E8  -  E15
  56 - 63 = E16 – E23
```

### Example

- if d0=47 then

```asm
    storei d0,(a1)
```

- would do the same as

```asm
    store e7,(a1)
```

- Value is modulo 64, so 64 is seen as 0.

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have no STOREI. It is new on the 68080.

## Do / Don't

- DON'T use an immediate `<vea>`.
